claims.claim: Introduced host distributions broadly expand reconstructed butterfly larval-resource geography, and observed host identities produce more expansion than same-plant-family, same-host-count alternatives.
claims.status: descriptive reconstruction plus post-hoc matched-host randomization
claims.evidence: 206/239 species expand; aggregate +54.9%. In conservative n=215, median observed-minus-null log expansion=0.140 and 156/215 exceed the null median.

claims.claim: Introduced-added host geography is enriched for independent contemporary butterfly occurrences that lie outside native host envelopes.
claims.status: independent geographic validation with post-hoc exact overlap null
claims.evidence: Full panel: 66/115 outside-native species x region observations recovered versus 38.0 expected; qualified panel: 49/61 versus 30.6 expected.

claims.claim: Family-level taxonomic host breadth only partly tracks geographic larval-resource breadth.
claims.evidence: rho=0.276 in n=239 and rho=0.398 in conservative n=215; 18 one-family butterflies occur in the upper quartile of geographic resource breadth.

claims.claim: The raw specialist-generalist gradient in host-contribution concentration is largely structural and is not interpreted as an independent mechanism.
claims.evidence: In n=191, raw rho family breadth vs effective contributors=0.492 and vs maximum share=-0.486; after controlling contributing-host count, rho=0.071 and -0.093.

claims.claim: Climate-associated filtering persists within contemporary host-resource opportunity even when comparisons are restricted within broad WGSRPD level-1 regions.
claims.status: independent cross-fit descriptive result plus post-hoc accessibility sensitivity
claims.evidence: Original n=24 median score=0.801; same-level1 n=23 median=0.798 and 21/23 >0.5.

claims.claim: The independent data do not support the pre-specified prediction that broader family-level diets weaken climate-associated filtering.
claims.evidence: partial rho=-0.166, one-sided p=0.2237, n=24; approximate 95% interval -0.54 to +0.26. Same-level1 sensitivity rho=+0.207, p=0.8232.

deprecated_v0_1_interpretation.claim: Family-level generalists independently assemble anthropogenic opportunity through more distributed host portfolios than specialists.
deprecated_v0_1_interpretation.reason: Concentration metrics are structurally bounded by contributing-host richness; conditional associations are weak after contributor count is controlled.
